validity.recommendation: Correct StartState/Province and EndState/Province to West Virginia (Marshall & Wetzel counties); the current values are a location field mix-up, not just missing refs.
validity.researcher_notes: Sheet currently carries StartState/Province='Clarington' (a village name, not a state), EndLocation='Ohio' (a state name sitting in the Location field), EndState/Province='Chatham' (not a recognized WV or OH place near this project). None of these three fields hold a valid US state except by accident. Both independent sources that discuss the project's geography place it entirely in West Virginia: XcL Midstream's own operations page states 'XcL ... operates in the premier region of the Appalachia basin in Marshall and Wetzel Counties, West Virginia' and that the Appalachia Connector Pipeline sits '...in Southwest Appalachia'; Kallanish Energy (independent trade press, 2017-06-15) reports XcL 'intends to build roughly 100 miles of pipelines in Marshall and Wetzel counties' and titles the piece 'Appalachia Connector Pipeline under construction in W.Va.' Neither source mentions Ohio at all. 'Clarington, Ohio' is a real village directly across the Ohio River from Marshall County, WV, so it's plausible someone conflated a nearby Ohio place-name with the pipeline's actual West Virginia location, but no source supports an Ohio endpoint for this specific project. I could not find independent confirmation of exact start/end towns within WV (XcL describes a county-level gathering footprint, not two fixed termini), so I'm proposing state-level corrections only and leaving StartLocation/EndLocation blank rather than inventing towns.

validity.recommendation: Set PipelineType = 'gathering' (currently blank). All independent sources describe this as a gas-gathering system, not a long-haul transmission trunk.
validity.researcher_notes: PipelineType is blank on the sheet. Kallanish Energy (2017) describes it plainly as 'natural gas-gathering pipelines' that 'collect dry natural gas and wet or liquids-rich natural gas and move it to five connections on interstate pipelines' -- i.e. a gathering system feeding transmission lines, not a transmission line itself. S&P Global Platts (2017-06-12) independently corroborates: XcL received a shipper commitment 'for its gathering and transport system.' XcL's own current operations page also frames the asset as two gathering sub-systems ('Lean System' dry gas, 'Rich System' rich/wet gas) with named interstate interconnects, consistent with a gathering classification. Recommend PipelineType='gathering' per controlled_vocab.md.

validity.recommendation: Capacity=2000 MMcf/d is not corroborated by any source found; verify against a more current operator disclosure before treating it as sourced.
validity.researcher_notes: No source I found states 2000 MMcf/d for this project. At launch (S&P Global Platts, 2017-06-12), XcL described a '1-Bcf/d dry gas header system' plus a '200 MMcf/d wet gas system' (1,200 MMcf/d combined design, with THQ Appalachia I initially committing to 600 MMcf/d dry + 200 MMcf/d wet). XcL's own current operations page (Wayback capture 2025-06-21) describes the mature system differently again: Lean (dry) System '3+ billion cubic feet of deliverability' (3,000+ MMcf/d) and Rich (wet) System '600+ MMCF/d of processing deliverability with potential to expand to 1 BCF/d.' None of these figures is 2000 MMcf/d on its own, and combining sub-systems gives either ~1,200 (2017 design) or ~3,600-4,000+ (current, if lean+rich are summed, which may not even be the right way to combine them since one is gathering deliverability and the other is processing deliverability). This is a genuine, material disagreement across two independent snapshots in time, not a corroboration -- flagging rather than proposing a replacement number, since I can't determine which (if any) figure the sheet's 2000 is derived from. Searched both citations in the harvested pool plus the operator's current site; did not find a discrete 2000 MMcf/d statement anywhere.

validity.researcher_notes: EXISTENCE: confirmed real, independent of GEM. Three independent, non-GEM sources -- XcL Midstream's own corporate site, Kallanish Energy (trade press), and S&P Global Platts (trade press) -- all name and describe the 'Appalachia Connector Pipeline' as a real XcL Midstream gas-gathering project in Marshall/Wetzel Counties, WV, with a signed anchor-shipper contract (THQ Appalachia I, a Tug Hill affiliate) and a 2018 target in-service date, matching the sheet's StartYear1=2018. This is not a GEM-only/hallucinated entity. NAMING: every independent source spells it 'Appalachia Connector Pipeline' (no 'n'); the sheet's title is 'Appalachian Connector Pipeline.' Worth adding 'Appalachia Connector Pipeline' to OtherEnglishNames as the operator's/press's actual spelling, though I'm not treating this as a hard error since GEM may deliberately normalize to 'Appalachian.' LENGTH CAVEAT: LengthKnown=52 mi is not directly stated by any source I found (Kallanish 2017: 'roughly 100 miles' planned system-wide; XcL's current site: ~35 mi lean + ~27 mi rich = ~62 mi in-service, with 60+/45+ mi planned per sub-system). 52 mi sits plausibly on the growth trajectory between the 2017 estimate and the 2025 in-service total, so I'm not flagging it as wrong, just unconfirmed -- a future pass with a dated XcL disclosure close to the sheet's 2022-10-14 LastUpdated could pin this down. DUPLICATE CHECK: compared against all 45 other rows in the batch 3 roster (Rover, NEXUS, Rockies Express, Eastern Shore, Mountaineer [both clusters], Empire, Vector, Algonquin, Columbia Gas Transmission, Dominion/EGTS, etc.) -- none describe XcL Midstream, Marshall/Wetzel Counties WV, or an Appalachia/Appalachian Connector system; no duplicate found. OPERATOR SITE NOW DEAD: xclmidstream.com no longer resolves (DNS NXDOMAIN as of 2026-09-08); last live Wayback capture is 2025-06-21, with regular captures 2020-2025 before that. This could mean a rebrand, acquisition, or a simple domain lapse -- not by itself an existence or status concern (the pipeline's own operating status doesn't depend on the company having a live website), but worth a corporate-ownership check on a future pass.
